situation.note: quit my job last week to go all in on our brand. no money yet but honestly ive never felt more alive. i want to stay like this and not lose this fire when it gets hard

understanding.emotion: alive and afraid of losing it
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call starting what is yours to build, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: The fire that feels alive now becomes, over seven days, a resolve that can survive the first hard month.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the fire as yours, not borrowed from the moment.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the feeling will fade, and that is when resolve must hold.
week_beats.story: A young builder who left security and faced the first dry month shows you how resolve survives without the feeling.

understanding.core_struggle: Has quit a job and gone all in on a brand, feeling more alive than ever, and wants to keep that fire when the first hard month arrives.
understanding.mirror: You quit the job, the brand is yours alone, and for the first time in a while you feel awake.
understanding.insight: You feel more alive than ever because the work is yours. What will test you is the month when the feeling fades and only the work remains.
understanding.mechanism_label: Starting what is yours to build

queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the feeling or looks sideways at the prize; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A young builder who left security to build something of their own, faced the first dry month, and kept going without the feeling.

understanding.life_context: A student or young worker under twenty-five with no income now; they quit a job last week to build a brand, and for the first time in a long while they feel fully alive.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
verse.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
verse.translation: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.

matched.label: I can't tell if continuing is discipline or stubbornness

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, just before the great war, telling him to do the work that fits his nature. He says that no work is perfect. Every task has flaws, just as fire always has smoke. The point is to keep doing your own work, not to abandon it because it is not perfect.
verse.for_you: You quit the job and are all in on the brand. That fire you feel is real. The work you chose fits you, even if it is messy. The smoke of doubt will come. Let the work itself be enough.
verse.try_today: Notice one small flaw in your work and keep going.
verse.scene_line: You are in the smoke of your own fire.
asks: How do I know if the work truly fits me?
Can I still build a brand if I am not perfect?

verse.speaker: Shandilya
verse.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शान्त उपासीत । अथ खलु क्रतुमयः पुरुषो यथाक्रतुरस्मिꣳल्लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति स क्रतुं कुर्वीत ॥
verse.line: A person is made of resolve. As you resolve in this life, so you become. So resolve well.
verse.translation: All this is Brahman; from it all arises, into it all dissolves, in it all breathes; so one should meditate on it calmly. A person is made of resolve. As one's resolve is in this world, so one becomes on departing. So let one form a resolve.
verse.meaning: Shandilya speaks to the student, laying out the core of who they are. A person is made of resolve. As you resolve in this life, so you become. So resolve well. This is the pattern underneath the work. The feeling of being alive is the beginning. The resolve is what you become, and that is the substance of the work itself.
verse.for_you: The work is yours and the feeling is real. The resolve is what you become, and that is the substance of the work itself. What you are building is a self that can stand on its own.
verse.try_today: Notice what part of the work feels like a real choice, not a habit.
verse.scene_line: You are standing at the edge of what you resolve to become.
asks: How do I know if my resolve is strong enough?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from a place of knowing what it costs to stay the course. He says that people will praise or blame, money will come or go, and death itself could arrive at any moment. Yet the steady do not move a step from the path of what is right. He is not promising that the path will be easy, but that the person who walks it steadily will not be thrown off by the noise of the world.
verse.for_you: You are in the thick of building your brand, and the outside world has no idea what you are doing. There will be praise and blame, and the money will not be regular. The steadfast do not step off the right path. You are building what is yours to build.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment of doubt today, and name the path anyway.
verse.scene_line: You are the struck ball that bounces back, still on the path.
asks: How do I know when the path is right?
How do I step off the path without losing what I have built?

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: ऐहिकः प्राक्तनं हन्ति प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनं बलात् । सर्वदा पुरुषस्पन्दस्तत्रानुद्वेगवाञ्जयी ॥
verse.line: Today's effort and yesterday's keep wrestling. Whoever stays calm through it wins.
verse.translation: Present effort overcomes the past, and the past can overpower the present. It is always a contest of human striving, and the one who stays calm wins.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

matched.label: I'm anxious about how things will turn out

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is speaking to a young Rama who has given up and is asking if he is doomed by fate. Vasishtha tells him that fate is only yesterday's effort, and his present effort can overcome it. It is a contest between past and present, and the one who stays calm and keeps striving wins.
verse.for_you: You quit your job last week and feel alive, but now the first hard month is here. The texts say your past effort shaped this moment, and your present effort shapes tomorrow. Stay calm and keep working. The resolve you are building now is who you are becoming.
verse.try_today: Notice one small sign of forward motion, no matter how tiny.
verse.scene_line: You are a young Rama who has stepped off the path, and now must turn back.
asks: How do I know if my past effort is strong enough to carry me?
Can I really overcome what I call fate?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.

words.en: cause of the fruit of action

verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

matched.label: I'm anxious about how things will turn out

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield. He tells him to fix his mind on the action and let go of the outcome. The work is his alone. The fruits of it belong to another. Do not let the fear of results stop you from doing what you know is right.
verse.for_you: You are building a brand and the feeling of being alive is strong right now. The first hard month will test that feeling. Do the work fully today, and let the results belong to something else.
verse.try_today: Do one piece of work for the brand with your full attention, then step away from checking its results.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the edge of your own action, with the outcome beyond your reach.
asks: How do I keep going when the results are not in my hands?
How do I know if I am doing enough?

verse.speaker: Janaka's doorkeeper
verse.setting: As Janaka sits lost in thought, his doorkeeper reminds him the day's work is waiting.
verse.sanskrit: शीघ्रमुत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते नियतं कार्यमाचर । न कालमतिवर्तन्ते महान्तः स्वेषु कर्मसु ॥
verse.line: Get up and do today's work. Great people don't let the hour slip by.
verse.translation: Rise quickly, bless you, and do your appointed work. The great do not let the time slip by in their own duties.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.for_you: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.

story.title: The missed deadline
story.story_hook: They came out of the cave to find that spring had already come, and their deadline had gone.
story.summary: The southern search party loses time in a magic cave and misses Sugriva's deadline. Angada rallies them once, then despairs, fearing punishment and certain he will be blamed. Hanuman reasons with him to return.
story.lesson: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

anchor.speaker: Angada
anchor.setting: The monkeys searching for Sita are exhausted and failing; young Angada rallies them.
anchor.sanskrit: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥
anchor.line: Keep working and the results will come. Sink into despair and it is hard to get back up.
anchor.translation: Those who keep working surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
anchor.why: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.
